properties.description: Minimalism is characterized by stripping music down to its fundamental features, which are then repeated and slowly changed over time. It is known for its use of simple rhythmic and melodic patterns.
properties.history: Minimalism emerged in the late 1960s as a reaction against the complexity of serialism and the randomness of aleatory music, both popular at that time. It was pioneered by composers such as Steve Reich, Philip Glass, and Terry Riley.
properties.performance: Can be solo or ensemble performance
properties.vocals: Can be either instrumental or include vocals

properties.description: Post-Minimalism is a category of music that describes an interrelated set of styles descended from minimalism, which share key stylistic features with minimalism, but move beyond its limitations. Typically, these pieces of music will have a clearly perceptible pulse, even when they eschew strong melodies or harmonic progressions, and are usually quieter than other music.
properties.history: Post-minimalism, a sub-style of minimal music, originated in the late 1970s as a reaction against the repetitiveness and austerity of minimalist music, incorporating more lyrical and expressive elements.
